key_insight: OmniLiDAR unifies multi-domain LiDAR synthesis into a single text-conditioned diffusion model, enabling controllable generation across diverse sensors and sensing conditions that previously required separate models.
problem_solved: Current diffusion-based LiDAR generators are trained per-dataset or per-sensor, forcing multiple specialized models and limiting scalable, controllable synthesis under heterogeneous distribution shifts; OmniLiDAR addresses the need for a single, flexible generator spanning multiple domains.
method: Build a unified text-conditioned diffusion backbone that models point/cloud distributions across datasets and sensors.
Introduce domain-conditioning (e.g., domain tokens/embeddings or prompts) and multi-domain training strategies to handle sensor-specific characteristics and distribution shifts within one model.
Train with mixed-domain supervision and domain-aware losses to preserve fidelity and diversity while enabling controllable synthesis by text or sensor prompt.
impact: OmniLiDAR reduces the engineering and maintenance cost of per-domain models, accelerates scalable simulation and synthetic-data generation for perception pipelines, and improves robustness to sensor and environmental variation—useful for data augmentation, benchmarking, and domain adaptation.
visual_elements: Diagram of the unified diffusion pipeline showing text/domain prompt input → shared diffusion backbone → multi-domain LiDAR outputs (different sensor styles).
Before/after grid of generated point clouds illustrating multiple sensing conditions (e.g., different beam patterns, weather, density).
Schematic comparing many single-domain models vs. one unified OmniLiDAR model (resource/maintenance savings).
Quantitative bar chart showing fidelity/diversity metrics (e.g., FID or task performance) across domains to demonstrate consistent performance.
paper_title: OmniLiDAR: A Unified Diffusion Framework for Multi-Domain 3D LiDAR Generation
paper_authors: Youquan Liu, Weidong Yang, Ao Liang, Xiang Xu, Lingdong Kong
